land.text: Joan's lands in the Comtat Venaissin, held by Alphonse, Count of Poitiers and Toulouse, and 'bequeathed to the Holy See on his death in 1271'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Toulouse row ends in 1249; the Comtat came to Alphonse and his wife Joan through the Toulouse inheritance (Alphonse page: 'they became rulers of Toulouse at Raymond's death in 1249'). The infobox dates are 'Acquired by papacy: 1271' and 'Annexed as a Papal state: 1274'; the map uses 1274.

land.text: the Comtat, annexed by the plebiscite of 14 September 1791 ('Reversed into France by plebiscite'); the Vaucluse department was made from it a few years later

successors.note: The papacy 'did not recognise this formally until 1814' (page), but the territory was French from 1791.

capitals.name: Venasque
capitals.note: Infobox 'Venasque (1274-1320)'; the Venasque page: 'In 1320 Venasque was replaced as capital of the Comtat by Carpentras.' Coordinates 43.9969 N, 5.1472 E as printed on the Venasque page.

capitals.name: Carpentras
capitals.note: Infobox 'Carpentras (1320-1791)'. Coordinates 44.0558 N, 5.0489 E as printed on the Carpentras page. Avignon was never the capital of the Comtat: it was a separate comtat run by a Cardinal Legate or Vice-Legate until it was joined in 1348.

correction.text: the Comtat Venaissin as a papal territory from 1274 (not 1272), without Avignon, which was a separate comtat until Pope Clement VI bought it from Joanna I in 1348; the 1272 shape already contains Avignon's cell

keyframe_review.note: 1272-1351, 2,109 km2 (8 cells). Page: 'The Comtat became a Papal territory in 1274' (infobox 'Annexed as a Papal state: 1274'); Alphonse's bequest dates from 1271. Avignon 'was administered by a Cardinal Legate' and was bought in 1348, so the cell at Avignon belongs from 1348 only. The page gives no area, so only the cell count (8 cells of about 250 km2) checks the 2,109 km2.

1352-1384, 2,390 km2 (9 cells): one cell east of Avignon (about 4.9 E, 44.1 N) is added to the 1272 shape. Avignon itself was bought in 1348 ('whereupon the two comtats were joined to form a unified papal enclave'); the page does not date the extra cell, so the shape stands as the enclave after the join.

1385-1481, 2,437 km2 (10 cells): one more cell (about 5.0 E, 44.2 N, north-east of Carpentras). No page opened dates a change in 1385; the Valreas exclave was 'purchased by Pope John XXII' (no date on the page). Kept as drawn, unverified for the extra cell.

1482-1672, 2,319 km2: the same cells as 1385 minus edge slivers. The page records no territorial change in these years; the French invasions of 1663 and 1668 are in the ledger as occupations, not as changes of border.
1673-1676, 2,132 km2, the same cell set as the neighbouring shapes; the change is a polygon-edge difference of about 190 km2, not a recorded border move.
1702-1705, 2,390 km2, the same cells; edge difference only, no page event.
1706-1787, 2,132 km2, the same cells; the French occupation of 1768-1774 did not change the border (ledger occupation events).

correction.text: unchanged shape, but it runs to September 1791 and not to 1790: 'Reversed into France by plebiscite: 14 September 1791'

keyframe_review.note: 1788-1790 in Cliopatria; the page dates the annexation to 14 September 1791, so the shape holds through 1791. The same cells as 1706-1787.

region.text: the Comtat Venaissin, the lands of Joan of Toulouse around Venasque and Carpentras, as a papal territory

ledger.note: 1274: the Comtat Venaissin becomes a papal territory. 'Alphonse bequeathed it to the Holy See on his death in 1271'; 'The Comtat became a Papal territory in 1274' (infobox 'Annexed as a Papal state: 1274'; 'Acquired by papacy: 1271'). The Alphonse page says Joan's lands in the Comtat 'became a papal territory' without a year and that Parlement invalidated her will in 1274; the Venasque page gives 1271. Capital Venasque.
1320: the capital moves from Venasque to Carpentras. 'Venasque ... replaced as capital by Carpentras in 1320' (Comtat page; the Venasque page says the same).

region.text: Avignon, sold to the papacy by Joanna I; 'the two comtats were joined to form a unified papal enclave'

ledger.note: 1348: the papacy buys Avignon. 'Avignon was sold to the papacy by Joanna I, Queen of Naples and Countess of Provence, in 1348' (infobox 'Avignon purchased from Joanna, Countess of Provence: 1348'); the Avignon page says Pope Clement VI bought it. Avignon kept its own administration under a Cardinal Legate. Cliopatria draws Avignon's cell in the Comtat from 1272.

region.text: the Comtat, 'invaded by French troops in 1663'

ledger.note: 1663: French troops occupy the Comtat. Infobox 'French occupation: 1663, 1668, 1768-1774'; text 'It was invaded by French troops in 1663, 1668 and 1768-1774.'
The page lists 1663 only and gives no end, so the occupation is bridged as lasting that year; the Comtat stayed papal. Page silent on the end.

region.text: the Comtat, 'invaded by French troops in ... 1668'

ledger.note: 1668: French troops occupy the Comtat again (same infobox line as 1663).
The page lists 1668 only and gives no end; bridged as that year. Page silent on the end.

region.text: the Comtat, occupied by French troops 1768-1774

ledger.note: 1768: France occupies the Comtat. 'It was invaded by French troops in 1663, 1668 and 1768-1774' (infobox 'French occupation: ... 1768-1774'). The Avignon page does not mention it.

region.text: the Comtat returned to papal rule

ledger.note: 1774: the French occupation ends (infobox 'French occupation: ... 1768-1774'); the page does not say how.

14 September 1791: the Comtat votes to join France. 'an unauthorized plebiscite, under pressure from French revolutionaries, was held and the inhabitants voted for annexation by France' (infobox 'Reversed into France by plebiscite: 14 September 1791'); the Avignon page: 'Papal control persisted until 1791'; the Carpentras page: 'Until 1791, Carpentras was part of the Papal States'. The papacy did not recognise it until 1814.

wars.name: French occupations of the Comtat Venaissin
wars.outcome: Three French invasions (1663, 1668 and 1768-1774) that each ended with the Comtat back under papal rule, until the plebiscite of 14 September 1791 gave it to France.
wars.note: The page gives only the years ('invaded by French troops in 1663, 1668 and 1768-1774'), not the causes or the ends of the first two; the ledger bridges those at confidence 1.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty or survey line for the Comtat's frontier with Provence, Orange and the Dauphine; the 8-10 cell shape is approximate throughout. Avignon, the Valreas exclave and the Orange enclaves make the real frontier more intricate than any shape.

notes: Cliopatria's nine shapes are one enclave of 8-10 cells; only the 1352 and 1385 steps add a cell and no page dates either, the later changes are polygon-edge differences. The 1272 shape already contains Avignon's cell although Avignon was a separate comtat until 1348 (ledger gain; keyframe 1272 removes it for 1274-1347). The pages give no start for the Valreas exclave ('purchased by Pope John XXII', undated; not in the ledger because no year is on the page). Dates disagree on the start: the infobox gives 1271 (Alphonse's bequest) and 1274 (annexed as a papal state); the Alphonse page says Parlement invalidated Joan's will in 1274, so the cession year rests on the Comtat page alone. The French occupations of 1663 and 1668 have no end year on the page (confidence 1 bridging, same year). Wikipedia gives no area. Cliopatria ends the polity in 1790; the page puts the annexation on 14 September 1791. The Comtat is placed in the 'italy' colour family as a papal territory (Papal States); the colour agent may prefer 'france'. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none used.
